We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will
be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission
on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service,
you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission
cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item which does
not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

II.  Flag Salute

III.  Approval of the Minutes of the regular meeting of March 8, 2022

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth
  Commission April 12, 2022

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:00 pm on April 12, 2022 at the
Alhambra Public Library Conference Room, 101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA.

Commission Members Present: D. Andrade, B. Gonzalez, T. Hernandez, Z. Oliva, M. Webster, J. Quach,
N. Quach

Commission Members Absent: J. Cooper, A. Gutierrez, M. Munson, L. Tran

Also present: Director of Parks & Recreation - Michael Macias, Deputy Director - Brie Houghton,
Program Coordinator - Frank Reyes

Flag Salute
Approval of Minutes
President N. Quach moved to approve the Minutes of March 8th, 2022 Adjourned Regular Meeting. Motioned
by Commissioner Z. Oliva and Seconded by Commissioner M. Webster the motion carried by unanimous vote.

Nomination and Election of President and Vice President of the Youth Commission
President N. Quach started the elections by self nominating for President. Commissioners Z. Oliva and
M. Webster followed with self nonminating for Vice President. Deputy Director Houghton, had the
Commissioner vote. The voting results were that N. Quach was named as President and Megan Webster as
Vice President of the Youth Commission.

Bunny Hop Walk, Arbor, and Other City Events
President N. Quach opened up by discussing the Bunny Hop event. An issue was mentioned that some of the
volunteers were not pleased with how they were treated by a City Staff. Both Deputy Director Brie Houghton
and Program Coordinator Frank Reyes expressed their empathy and concern for the matter. Frank Reyes
elaborated on the matter, by expressing his gratitude toward the volunteers. He also shared the expectations of
the volunteers as some volunteers did not stay for the entirety of the event which resulted in City Staff and the
volunteers compensating for the lack of coverage. Overall the issue was resolved, the Commission specified
going forward there would be better communication regarding how roles will be delegated and what's expected
of the volunteers. The Arbor Day event was discussed including the revised time. Also mentioned was the 626
Golden Streets event on May 1, 2022, which is from 7 AM to 4 PM operated by Active SGV. The Commission
was extended an opportunity to attend. A headcount was taken on who was going to attend the event. Director
Macias gave his thoughts and input on how the event could aid in promoting the 2022 Youth Summit.

Community Engagement with the Seniors and Tech Talk
President N. Quach led the discussion on the importance of keeping Tech Talk for the senior citizen community
and how it has helped and how it's led to engagement with the commissioners and community. Deputy Director
Houghton expressed how the seniors value the time spent in Tech talk. The Commission discussed possible
future events with the seniors. Deputy Director Houghton asked if Youth Commission would be interested in
assisting in any future programs and events that the city holds for the Senior Citizens.

Youth Summit
President N. Quach had put together a timeline for the Youth Summit which was to be finalized by March 25,
2022. Consisted of keynote speakers, and donors' recommendations. Alvin Lee of Generation Up,
Superindentent of Los Angeles County Office of Education, and the Student Board Member of the California
Board of Education.
 President Quach also mentioned how some guest speakers would be participating from local Organizations
and businesses as well as Councilmembers, highlighting Sasha Renee Perez. President N. Quach stated that
Councilmember Perez would be a great representation of the Youth Summit being that she was the youngest
Mayor in the history of the city. Commission Oliva emphasized the importance of having a stable timeline
as well as a description of what will be occurring during the Youth Summit. Commission Webster proposed
having all the Documents for the Summit saved on Google Drive so that all Commission Members have
easier access to the files. Director of Parks & Recreation Macias gave the Commission a few suggestions on
how to divide the workload. Director Macias suggested having a lead on specific tasks that can be assigned
to individuals would help towards creating a program for the Youth Summit. Commission Oliva discussed
how the Youth Survey should be distributed at the Summit itself as long as a member of the commission
takes the lead on said task to make sure it is completed. Commission Gonzalez suggested using a QR code
for the survey for the attendees to scan and complete when they have time. Program Coordinator Frank
Reyes gave some suggestions to the Commission on how they could organize the activities in the Event
including handing out the Survey to the attending Youth. He also suggested using a Responsibility Matrix
that could be presented as a flow chart of all the tasks, who’s leading them, and what deadlines need to be
met if necessary. Deputy Director Houghton mentioned that having a group text chat for the Commission
would be useful in updating the members with the completed task and any pertinent information regarding
the event. Commission Andrade stated that she had created a google drive for the event and that she had
shared it with the other members of the Commission. She also volunteered to create a group chat for the
members of the Commission to keep updated with any pertinent information regarding the event.
Commission Webster presented that now would be the best time to assign the tasks and the rest of the
committee members agreed. The task was assigned to the Commission members for the Youth Summit as
follows: N. Quach – Program and Agenda, Z. Oliva – Booths and Outreach, J. Quach and B. Gonzalez –
Survey and QR code, Z. Oliva and N. Quach – Layout, T. Hernandez – Donations, D. Andrade – Flyer and
Publicity, M. Webster & D. Andrade – Volunteers, All Members Youth of the year Award, Leads on Day of
Event – D. Andrade and M. Webster.

Oral Communications
None

Commision Orals
Program Coordinator Frank Reyes read two emails written by Alhambra High School students speaking
highly of President N. Quach’s abilities, accomplishments and their hope he will be reelected to the same
position. President N. Quach continued to Commission Orals where Commission B. Gonzalez asked if
there was any update with the Alhambra Skate Park. President N. Quach stated funding for the Skate Park
at this moment was diverted. He also thanked the City staff for all their help and support to the
Commission.

Adjournment
President N. Quach motioned adjournedment at 7:27 PM
